q: Brasília, considered the biggest planning exercise of the 20th century, was completed within four years using how many workers?
n: 600,000 workers finished Brasília within 4 years. (Source: Lucio Costa, p.99)

q: Which architect was commissioned by Pope Sixtus V to prepare a street plan for Rome, marking key points in the city with tall obelisks as visual accents?
n: Domenico Pontana was commissioned by Pope Sixtus V to prepare and establish a street plan/framework for the growth of Rome, marking key points with tall obelisks. (Source: Rome 1500s, p.85)

q: English social reformer Robert Owen constructed an industrial village at New Lanark based on the concept of:
n: Owen constructed and operated an industrial village at New Lanark, a social and manufacturing community conceptualized as the "Village of Unity and Mutual Cooperation." (Source: 1799, p.86)

q: Wright and Stein's regional planning approach proposed a core of constellations of smaller communities, exemplified by which New Jersey community?
n: The core of constellations of smaller communities is exemplified by Radburn, New Jersey. (Source: Henry Wright and Clarence Stein, p.93)

q: British-born architect Ralph Erskine built the remarkable Byker Wall, a redevelopment housing project designed for:
o: Maximum density regardless of resident input
n: The Byker Wall was designed for continuous dialogue with the residents. (Source: Ralph Erskine, p.100)

q: The People's Homesite and Housing Corporation (PHHC) was established primarily to address:
o: Growing housing needs, especially in urban centers
n: PHHC was established to address growing housing needs, especially in urban centers, and was notably involved in developing Quezon City and large housing subdivisions. (Source: Philippine Republic, p.104)

q: Haussmann's rebuilding of Paris made the city a "City of Lights" and became the model for which American movement, later adopted by Daniel Burnham?
n: Paris became the model for the American City Beautiful Era, adopted by Daniel Burnham. (Source: Paris 1800s, p.86)

s: New Communities Built Around New Factories
q: George Cadbury relocated his chocolate factory to Bournville outside Birmingham (1879–1895), notable for being open to workers:
n: Bournville was open to workers regardless of race or religion. (Source: New Communities, p.90)

q: In "The New Exploration: A Philosophy of Regional Planning," Benton Mackaye coined the interdependent concepts of the "townless highway" and the:
n: Mackaye spoke of the "townless highway" and "highwayless town" as mutually interdependent. (Source: Benton Mackaye, p.94)

q: Patrick Geddes coined the term "conurbation" to describe:
n: Geddes coined "conurbation," meaning a conglomeration of town aggregates. (Source: Patrick Geddes, p.92)

q: Thomas Adams directed the 8-volume 1928 survey for the New York City Metropolitan Area (RPAA/RPA), which was criticized for its limits on:
n: The 8-volume survey directed by Adams was criticized for its limits on physical scope. (Source: Thomas Adams, p.94)

q: Norbert Wiener's ideas were instrumental in changing the planning paradigm from production of blueprints towards planning as:
o: A single master plan drawn once
A continuous series of controls over the development of an area
n: Wiener helped shift planning from static blueprints to continuous controls over development, aided by devices that model or simulate the development process. (Source: Norbert Wiener, p.95–96)

q: Jane Jacobs argued that there was nothing wrong with high urban densities of people as long as they did not entail:
n: Jacobs argued high densities were fine if they did not entail overcrowding in buildings, and prescribed mixed functions/land uses and mixed-age blocks to serve different purposes and schedules. (Source: Jane Jacobs, p.101)

q: The Convent (Convento) in a Spanish colonial town was:
o: The residence of priests or friars, typically attached to or near the church
n: The Convento was the residence of priests or friars, typically attached to or near the church. (Source: Spanish Period — Key Elements, p.102)

q: Patrick Geddes wrote "Cities in Evolution" in which year?
n: Geddes wrote Cities in Evolution in 1915 (earlier works were City Development in 1904 and Civics as Applied Sociology in 1905). (Source: Patrick Geddes, p.92)

q: American Edgar Chambless proposed a city with all vehicles running on:
n: Chambless proposed a city with all vehicles running on the rooftops of a continuous building. (Source: 1910, p.87)

q: Rome in the 1500s was confronted with problems of circulation, defense, water supply, and:
n: Rome faced problems of circulation, defense, water supply, and sanitation, prompting Popes to undertake civic improvement projects. (Source: Rome 1500s, p.85)

s: Modern Architecture and Planning — Eliel Saarinen
q: In 1943, Eliel Saarinen wrote "The City," proposing:
n: "The City" (1943) proposed the decentralization of large cities. (Source: Eliel Saarinen, p.98)

q: During the American Era, there were no local planning institutions, and Filipino planners were trained:
o: At the UP Institute of Planning
n: There were no local planning institutions in this era; Filipino planners were trained abroad. (Source: American Era, p.103)

q: Viennese architect Christopher Alexander developed the idea that for things to become alive and beautiful, it is necessary for people to be:
o: Directly involved in the act of construction
n: Alexander believed people must be directly involved in the act of construction, rather than fiddling, for things to become alive and beautiful. (Source: Christopher Alexander, p.100)

q: According to Geddes, the stages in the creation of conurbations follow the sequence:
o: Inflow → Build up → Backflow (central slums) → Sprawling mass
n: The stages are Inflow, Build up, Backflow (center slums), then Sprawling mass (central blight). (Source: Patrick Geddes, p.92)

q: Which of the following was NOT one of the recognizable Marcos-era Philippine projects mentioned in the source?
n: Radburn, New Jersey is a U.S. New Communities Movement project, not one of the Marcos-era Philippine projects (Metro Manila Strategic Plan, Tondo Foreshore Project, BLISS housing) listed in the source. (Source: Marcos Regime, p.104)

q: The Spanish "reduccion system" was a policy of gathering scattered indigenous populations into centralized villages or towns primarily to facilitate administration, tax collection, evangelization, and:
n: The reduccion system facilitated administration, tax collection, evangelization, and social control. (Source: Spanish Period — Urban Impact, p.103)

q: Constantine Doxiadis published his "Ekistic Grids," a system for:
o: Recording planning data and ordering the planning process
n: The Ekistic Grids were a system for recording planning data and ordering the planning process. (Source: Constantine Doxiadis, p.96)

q: Spanish colonial settlements in the Philippines were called "pueblos" (towns/townships), structured around what system?
n: Pueblos were structured around the reduccion system. (Source: Spanish Period, p.102)

q: Daniel Burnham, called the "Father of American City Planning" and "Prophet of the City Beautiful Movement," wrote which two notable works?
o: Cities in Evolution and Garden Cities of Tomorrow
Plan for Chicago (1909) and Planning the Region of Chicago (1956)
Broadacre City and The Disappearing City
The City in History and Technics and Civilization
n: Burnham wrote the Plan for Chicago (1909) and Planning the Region of Chicago (1956), his greatest achievement being the Chicago Plan of 1909. (Source: Daniel Burnham, p.90–91)

q: Working under a commission chaired by Stein, Henry Wright produced a report explaining how New York transformed from a city of small trade centers into a financial and managerial center, titled:
o: "The Report of the Commission in Housing and Regional Planning for the State of New York"
n: Wright, working under Stein's commission, produced this report on New York's development. (Source: Henry Wright and Clarence Stein, p.93)

s: Conservationist & Park Movement — Frederick Law Olmstead
q: Frederick Law Olmstead, the "Father of Landscape Architecture" associated with the American park system, designed which famous New York park?
n: Olmstead is associated with the American park system and designed Central Park, New York, among other projects. (Source: Conservationist & Park Movement, p.87–88)

q: The Metro Manila Commission (MMC), established in 1975 under PD 824 to centralize governance of Metro Manila, was chaired during its early years by:
n: The MMC was chaired by Imelda Marcos during its early years. (Source: Marcos Regime, p.104–105)

q: Medieval towns typically grew around which two protective/organizing centers?
o: A fortress or a river crossing only
A university or a cathedral only
n: Growth of towns around either a monastery or a castle relied on protective town walls or fortification for security. (Source: Medieval Times, p.84–85)

q: Leslie Patrick Abercrombie (1879–1957), British, pioneered regional planning for the Doncaster area (1920–1922) and East Kent, and was involved in the:
n: Abercrombie was involved in the Greater London Plan, using open space as a structuring element. (Source: Leslie Patrick Abercrombie, p.95)

q: Scottish architect James Craig planned linear new towns interconnected by plazas, grid houses, and open spaces on a plateau overlooking which city?
n: James Craig planned linear new towns for Edinburgh, with interconnected plazas, grid houses, and open spaces on a plateau overlooking the city. (Source: 1767, p.86)

q: In the 1930s, Frank Lloyd Wright wrote "The Disappearing City" and later "Broadacres," proposing that every family live on:
n: Wright proposed every family live on an acre of land, with the city built by its inhabitants using mass-produced components. (Source: Frank Lloyd Wright, p.99)

q: Albert Speer (1905–1981) was tasked by Hitler with planning the reconstruction of:
n: Albert Speer was tasked by Hitler to plan the reconstruction of Berlin. (Source: The City Beautiful Era, p.88)

q: The 1909 Chicago Plan was heavily criticized as "centro-centrist," planned as an aristocratic city for merchant princes, with scant attention to:
n: Mumford castigated the plan as cosmetic, comparing it to totalitarian planning; health and sanitation were almost nowhere addressed and it devoted scant attention to zoning. (Source: Daniel Burnham, p.91)

q: The Market (Tiangge or Pamilihan) in the plaza complex was located near the plaza for accessibility and served as a space for trade, taxation, and:
n: The market was a space for trade, taxation, and economic control. (Source: Spanish Period — Key Elements, p.102)

q: Richard Sennett cited the demolition of which housing project — blown up 17 years after being built (1972) — as a symbol of what was perceived as wrong with urban renewal?
n: The Pruitt-Igoe Housing Project, 33 identical blocks with 2,800 apartments (completed 1955–56, designed by Minoru Yamasaki), was demolished in 1972 and became a symbol of what was wrong with urban renewal. (Source: Richard Sennett, p.100)

q: Rectilinear/gridded land plotting associated with the plow in the Ancient World was used in all of the following EXCEPT:
n: The source lists ancient Greek towns, Roman colonial outposts, and Indian, Chinese, and pre-Columbian cities — not medieval fortress towns, which belong to a later period. (Source: Ancient World, p.84)

q: Leon Battista Alberti is remembered as the foremost early theoretician for his concept of:
n: Alberti is remembered for his "ideal cities" — star-shaped plans with streets radiating from a central point. (Source: Renaissance, p.85)

q: John Gwynn's 1766 plan "London and Westminster Improved" heralded what era of building in London?
n: The plan heralded a Golden Age of building London. (Source: 1766, p.86)

q: The Home Financing Corporation (HFC) provided long-term financing for housing, including:
n: HFC provided long-term financing for housing, including home mortgages and loans. (Source: Philippine Republic, p.104)

q: Italian futurist Antonio Sant'Elia's "La Città Nuova" provided a vision of an enormous metropolis based on:
o: Motion, with vertical and horizontal circulation in every design element
n: Sant'Elia's vision was based on motion, with every element of its design implying vertical and horizontal circulation. (Source: Antonio Sant'Elia, p.87)

s: Modern Architecture and Planning — Eliel Saarinen
q: Eliel Saarinen's prize-winning plan for Helsinki featured an overall circulation pattern whose elements suited the:
n: Saarinen's Helsinki plan featured orderly, distinct community open space with a circulation pattern suited to the island and bay topography. (Source: Eliel Saarinen, p.98)

q: Constantine Doxiadis approached town planning as a science incorporating contributions from sociologists, geographers, economists, and other disciplines, calling this total rational and human approach:
n: Doxiadis called his approach "Ekistics" — the science of human settlements. (Source: Constantine Doxiadis, p.96)

q: Le Corbusier's "La Ville Radieuse" (Radiant City), proposed in 1993 per the source's outline, aimed to decongest city centers by:
o: Increasing density by building high on a small part of the total ground area
Spreading population evenly at low density
Relocating all industry to the countryside
n: La Ville Radieuse aimed to decongest centers by increasing density through high building on a small part of the total ground area. (Source: Le Corbusier, p.98)

q: Houses of the Principalia (local elite) were typically located closest to the plaza, because their proximity symbolized:
n: Principalia houses were located closest to the plaza, symbolizing power and prestige. (Source: Spanish Period — Key Elements, p.102)

q: Architect-theorist Claude Nicolas Ledoux's principal work, Chaux, was a town designed for:
n: Ledoux's principal work was Chaux, a town for salt workers in France, advocating informal grouping of houses and an ideal plan for workers' self-sufficiency. (Source: Early 19th Century, p.86)

s: Conservationist & Park Movement — Frederick Law Olmstead
q: Olmstead's 1880 plan connecting a system of parks in Boston is known as:
n: Olmstead created The Emerald Necklace Plan for Boston in 1880. (Source: Conservationist & Park Movement, p.88)

q: In Roman town planning, the "perfected enclosed urban and architectural space" typically featured colonnaded plazas ending with:
n: Perfected enclosed urban and architectural space refers to colonnaded plazas with a temple or basilica at the end of the space. (Source: Ancient Rome, p.84)

q: According to Kenzo Tange, once a city grows beyond 2 or 3 million, vital communication becomes inefficient in which type of city form?
o: A radiocentric city form created by spontaneous growth
n: Tange held that beyond 2–3 million, communication becomes inefficient in a radiocentric city form created by spontaneous growth. (Source: Kenzo Tange, p.99)

q: "CCPC," one of the planning institutions created in this period, stands for:
n: CCPC stands for the Capital City Planning Commission. (Source: Commonwealth Period, p.103)

q: Which planning-education institutions were created during the Marcos Regime?
o: The UP Institute of Planning and the Philippine Institute of Environmental Planners
n: The Marcos Regime saw the creation of the UP Institute of Planning and the Philippine Institute of Environmental Planners. (Source: Marcos Regime, p.104)

s: Town & Country Planning Act of 1947 in Britain
q: The Town and Country Planning Act of 1958 in Britain was essentially spatial, concerned with the spatial impact of many kinds of problems and:
o: The spatial coordination of many different policies
n: It was concerned with spatial impact of problems and the spatial coordination of many different policies. (Source: Town & Country Planning Act, p.95)

q: Pierre Charles L'Enfant, a French American engineer, is known for preparing the plan for:
n: L'Enfant prepared the plan for Washington, D.C. (Source: Renaissance era entries, p.85)

q: During the Marcos Regime, in terms of economic development, the Philippines ranked as:
n: In terms of economic development, the Philippines was no. 2 in Southeast Asia during this period. (Source: Marcos Regime, p.104)

q: French architect Tony Garnier designed a hypothetical industrial town with a definite center and a linear structure emphasizing zoning and separation of urban functions, called:
n: Garnier designed "Une Cité Industrielle," anticipating modern zoning through separation of city parts and urban functions. (Source: 1901, p.87)

q: Regional planning is said to have started with Patrick Geddes (1854–1932), whose ideas derived from Scottish culture are summed up in the famous dictum:
o: "The city is a machine for living"
n: "Survey before Plan" comes from Geddes. (Source: Patrick Geddes, p.91)

s: Ancient Greece (500–400 B.C.) — Hippodamus of Miletus
q: Who is the Greek architect who planned Priene and Piraeus, emphasizing geometric designs and the grid pattern of streets?
n: Hippodamus of Miletus, called the Father of Town Planning, planned Priene and Piraeus with geometric designs and gridiron streets. (Source: Ancient Greece, p.84)

q: The City Beautiful movement's most spectacular manifestations occurred between 1910 and 1935, eventually giving way to city functional concepts that included:
n: The movement gave way to city functional concepts that included zoning. (Source: The City Beautiful Era, p.88)

q: Medieval town street patterns generally featured:
o: Radial streets with a central piazza
n: Towns were generally unplanned, organically evolving with an irregular street pattern, and predominance of abbeys and cathedrals indicated church influence and control. (Source: Medieval Times, p.85)

q: The Mineral Reservations Development Board was created under which presidential decree during the Marcos Regime?
n: The Mineral Reservations Development Board was created under PD 1305. (Source: Marcos Regime, p.104)

q: Japanese architect-planner Kenzo Tange's plan for Tokyo emphasized the role of which factor as a determinant of urban form?
n: Tange's plan for Tokyo emphasized circulation as a determinant of urban form. (Source: Kenzo Tange, p.99)

q: The Human Settlements Regulatory Commission (HSRC), renamed from HSC in 1978 under Presidential Decree No. 1396, took on regulatory powers focusing on land use, zoning, and:
n: HSRC focused on land use, zoning, and building regulations, approving subdivision and condominium plans and issuing development permits. (Source: Marcos Regime, p.104)

q: Frank Lloyd Wright's Broadacre City, conceived in 1924, symbolized his rejection of finance capital, landlordism, and:
n: Broadacre City symbolized rejection of finance capital and landlordism, an anarchist rejection of big government, while believing in the liberating effects of new technologies. (Source: Frank Lloyd Wright, p.99)

q: Which of the following was NOT one of the four functions of the plaza described in the source?
n: The plaza's functions listed are Social, Political, Economic, and Religious — an industrial function is not mentioned. (Source: Spanish Period — Functions of the Plaza, p.102–103)

s: New Communities Built Around New Factories
q: Robert Owen's New Lanark experimental industrial settlement (1800–1810) provided which feature not common in industrial towns of the era?
o: Communal living and central heating, with private lodging for families with children under 3
n: New Lanark had 1,000-strong communities with residence near the workplace, communal living for old and young, central heating, and private lodging for families with children under 3. (Source: New Communities, p.90)

q: Which institution, formed after WWII, was the main government body responsible for national development planning and the precursor to what later became NEDA?
n: The NPC was the main government body responsible for national development planning and precursor to NEDA. (Source: Philippine Republic, p.103)

q: The first garden city, established in 1902 about 35 miles from London and planned by Barry Parker and Raymond Unwin, was:
n: In 1902, a garden city was established in Letchworth, 35 miles from London, planned by Barry Parker and Raymond Unwin. (Source: Ebenezer Howard, p.88)

q: Urban planning saw a shift back to local governance and participatory processes, formalized through the:
o: Urban Development and Housing Act of 1992
n: This period saw economic instability and discontinuity, with urban planning shifting back to local governance via the Local Government Code (LGC) of 1991. (Source: Aquino Regime, p.104)

q: Unlike the MMC, the MMDA has a "unique status" in that it coordinates with LGUs but does NOT have:
n: MMDA's unique status is that it coordinates with LGUs but does not have legislative authority over them, and has limited enforcement powers compared to the MMC. (Source: Aquino/post-EDSA Era, p.105)

q: The Human Settlements Commission (HSC) was established in 1975 under which presidential decree, to coordinate national efforts in urban development and housing?
n: HSC was established in 1975 under Presidential Decree No. 933. (Source: Marcos Regime, p.104)

q: Benton Mackaye, originally a forester, viewed the nation's natural divisions as:
o: River drainage areas, not state lines
n: Mackaye saw the nation as a series of component parts whose natural divisions were river drainage areas, not state lines. (Source: Benton Mackaye, p.94)

q: The basic socio-political unit during the Pre-Spanish Period, composed of 30–100 families ruled by kinship, was called:
n: The basic socio-political unit was the barangay, composed of 30–100 families ruled by kinship. (Source: Pre-Spanish Period, p.102)

q: What agricultural tool's widespread use gave rise to rectilinear plotting suited to the needs of agricultural societies in the Ancient World?
n: Rectilinear plotting used the plow, suited for land division for crop planning and land plotting after a flood along the Nile, Tigris, and Euphrates. (Source: Ancient World, p.84)

s: Ancient Greece (500–400 B.C.) — Hippodamus of Miletus
q: In ancient Greek town planning, which urban element consisted of buildings serving as facades to form an enclosed urban space, grouped around a central open space?
n: The Agora's buildings served as facades forming an enclosed urban space, grouped around a central open space. (Source: Ancient Greece, p.84)

q: Lewis Mumford urged that the fundamental needs of society be the basis for the judicious use of:
n: Mumford urged that fundamental needs be the basis for judicious use of technological power, recognizing the physical limitations of human settlements. (Source: Lewis Mumford, p.97)

q: In his "Codex Atlanticus," Leonardo da Vinci sketched a new urban planning concept suited for which city, involving a river divided into 6 or 7 branches?
n: Da Vinci described a new urban planning concept suited for Milan, sketching a city straddling a river with its upstream divided into 6–7 branches rejoining below the city. (Source: Rome 1500s, p.85)

q: The New Communities' Movement's rallying cry was to produce not only better homes, but:
n: The movement's rallying cry was to produce better communities, not just better homes, with community problem issues discussed openly among planners. (Source: New Communities' Movement, p.97)

q: Walter Burley Griffin (1875–1973) designed which capital city?
n: Walter Burley Griffin designed the Canberra plan. (Source: The City Beautiful Era, p.88)

q: In the Plaza Complex, which structure was usually the largest and most dominant, often located on the east side to face the setting sun and symbolizing the central role of the Catholic Church?
n: The Church was usually the largest and most dominant structure, often facing the setting sun and symbolizing the Church's central role. (Source: Spanish Period — Key Elements, p.102)

q: Daniel Burnham was commissioned during the American Era to prepare plans for Manila and which new summer capital?
n: Burnham's most significant projects were the remaking of Manila and the creation of an entirely new summer capital at Baguio. (Source: American Era, p.103)

q: According to the source, Rome became the first city with a population of one million by what year?
n: Rome was the first city with a million population, reached in 3 A.D. (Source: Ancient Rome, p.84)

q: Russian geographer Peter Kropotkin's "Fields, Factories, and Workshops" advocated combining agriculture and brainwork with:
n: Kropotkin's book combined agriculture and brainwork with manual work, and suggested electricity could allow towns to be built anywhere, advocating minimal government and maximum self-sufficiency. (Source: 1899, p.87)

q: The Ramos Administration activated the Environmental Planning Board under which body?
n: The Ramos Administration activated the Environmental Planning Board under the PRC. (Source: Ramos Administration, p.105)

q: During the Commonwealth Period, planning institutions such as NUPC, CCPC, and RPB were created, bridging colonial planning with:
n: This period bridged colonial planning with Filipino leadership, laying the groundwork for local urban governance. (Source: Commonwealth Period, p.103)

q: Which Roman architect wrote the 10-volume treatise "De Arkitektura," treating architecture and town design as a single theme?
n: Vitruvius's 10-volume treatise "De Arkitektura" related Roman architecture and town design experience as a single theme. (Source: Ancient Rome / Vitruvius, p.84)

q: Vitruvius's treatise laid the foundation of theoretical design thinking by addressing all of the following EXCEPT:
o: Location of streets relative to prevailing wind
n: Vitruvius addressed street orientation to wind, siting of public buildings, testing of drinking water, and design of plazas — steel-frame skyscrapers did not exist in his era. (Source: Ancient Rome / Vitruvius, p.84)

q: Massive reconstruction efforts in the post-WWII Philippine Republic period were especially concentrated in:
n: Massive reconstruction efforts were especially concentrated in Metro Manila. (Source: Philippine Republic, p.103)

q: Thomas Adams (1871–1940), one of the founding fathers of British Town Planning, served as the first general manager of:
n: Adams was first general manager of Letchworth Garden City. (Source: Thomas Adams, p.94)

q: Buckminster Fuller's "Inventory of World Resources — Human Trends and Needs" (1963) assessed the world's production and productive energy and suggested it be turned to man's:
n: Fuller assessed current world production/energy and suggested how it could be turned to man's complete advantage. (Source: Buckminster Fuller, p.96–97)

q: Charles Abrams saw housing as one of the prime fields for solving urban problems, writing:
o: "Man's Struggle for Shelter in an Urbanizing World" (1964)
n: Abrams wrote "Man's Struggle for Shelter in an Urbanizing World" (1964), discussing housing's prime role in urban development and policy. (Source: Charles Abrams, p.96)

s: New Communities Built Around New Factories
q: George Pullman, U.S. railroad engineer and inventor of Pullman cars, built his model industrial town outside Chicago (from 1880) on how many acres of wetland?
n: Pullman's model industrial town outside Chicago occupied 4,000 acres of wetland. (Source: New Communities, p.90)

q: Ebenezer Howard showed how workable, livable towns could be formed within the capitalist framework through the:
n: Howard's Social City concept involved decentralized employment, polycentric settlements, garden cities, and suburban expansion. (Source: Ebenezer Howard, p.88)

q: Antonio Kayanan, referenced in the source as the "first Filipino planner," is associated with which era of national planning?
o: The Philippine Republic (post-WWII) era, leading planning for Manila, Quezon City, and other cities
n: The source credits Antonio Kayanan, the first Filipino planner, with leading national planning during the Philippine Republic period, including plans for Manila and Quezon City. (Source: Philippine Republic, p.103)

q: The Radburn idea created a series of "superblocks" — islands of green bordered by homes and skirted by peripheral auto roads — connected by pedestrian ways called:
n: The Radburn idea's pedestrian ways were called greenways, interconnecting open green spaces within each superblock. (Source: New Communities' Movement, p.97)

q: Le Corbusier was criticized for shifting from a planning style toward an architectural style preoccupied with visual form, symbolism, and aesthetics, in a plan considered impervious to the economic and human considerations of which country's population?
n: The source notes his plan was completely impervious to the economic and human considerations of the Indian population. (Source: Le Corbusier, p.98)

q: HLURB was merged into which department in 2019?
o: Department of Interior and Local Government
Department of Human Settlements and Urban Development (DHSUD)
Department of Public Works and Highways
n: HLURB was merged into DHSUD in 2019. (Source: Aquino Regime, p.104)

s: The Regional Planning Association of America (RPAA)
q: The Regional Planning Association of America (RPAA), founded in 1923 from the close association of Mumford, Stein, MacKaye, and others, published a group manifesto called:
n: The RPAA published "Survey," one of the most important documents in planning history, devoted to the concept of the region. (Source: RPAA, p.93)

q: Architect Lucio Costa's plan did not include a single population projection, economic analyses, land use schedule, model, or mechanical drawing, yet was awarded the commission for:
n: Lucio Costa's scheme, despite lacking these typical elements, was awarded for Brasília, the new interior capital replacing an overburdened Rio de Janeiro. (Source: Lucio Costa, p.98–99)

q: The Housing and Land Use Regulatory Board (HLURB) worked with LGUs to guide the preparation of:
n: HLURB worked with LGUs to guide comprehensive land use plans (CLUPs), part of its devolution of oversight functions. (Source: Aquino Regime, p.104)

q: The Garden City Movement concept was a response to which type of city, proposing to disperse people into new, self-contained constellations of towns in open countryside?
n: The concept responded to the Victorian City by exploring the dispersal of people to new self-contained constellations of new towns built in open countryside. (Source: Garden City Movement, p.88)

q: John Nash's ambitious 1811 London concept connected the center of the city to a park at the city's edge via a grand avenue, resulting in the design of:
o: Regent Street and Regent Park Crescent
n: Nash's plan and carried-out work resulted in Regent Street, Regent Park, and Crescent. (Source: 1811, p.86)

q: In Alberti's "ideal cities," the star-shaped plan with radiating streets was usually proposed for a:
n: The designs were usually proposed for a church, palace, or castle, with curved streets conforming to topography. (Source: Renaissance, p.85)

q: Le Corbusier unveiled his "Ville Contemporaine" in 1922 as a hypothetical plan for a city of how many people?
n: The "Ville Contemporaine" was a hypothetical plan for a city of 3 million people, exploiting technology. (Source: Le Corbusier, p.98)

q: According to Daniel Burnham, the ideal city in the City Beautiful Era was a totally designed system of circulation arteries, parks, and civic center building blocks including all of the following EXCEPT:
n: The civic center blocks listed are city hall, a country house, a library, an opera house, a museum, and a plaza — a factory district is not mentioned. (Source: The City Beautiful Era, p.88)

q: American architect-planner Clarence A. Perry's 1929 book, "The Neighborhood Unit," discussed organizing towns into cohesive neighborhoods based on the natural catchment area of community facilities such as:
n: Perry's neighborhood principle was based on the natural catchment area of facilities such as a primary school and shops. (Source: Clarence A. Perry, p.97–98)

q: French planner Eugene Henard's "The Cities of the Future" envisioned buildings on stilts, traffic circles, and:
n: Henard's vision included buildings on stilts, traffic circles, and airplane rooftop landings. (Source: Eugene Henard, p.87)

q: The Ramos Administration's economic development program focused on infrastructure such as power, telecom, LRT, MRT, flyovers, ports, and airports, alongside a mushrooming of:
n: This period saw major infrastructure projects and the mushrooming of shopping malls throughout the country, plus the emergence of mixed-use development. (Source: Ramos Administration, p.105)

q: Lewis Mumford's influential 1961 book on the history and prospects of the city is titled:
n: Mumford wrote "The City in History" (1961). (Source: Lewis Mumford, p.97)

q: Known as a "Master Builder," Robert Moses was in charge of the implementation of:
n: Robert Moses, Master Builder, was in charge of implementing the New York Plan. (Source: Robert Moses, p.95)

q: The Metropolitan Manila Development Authority (MMDA), successor to the MMC, was created in 1995 under which law?
n: MMDA was created in 1995 under Republic Act No. 7924. (Source: Aquino/post-EDSA Era, p.105)

s: New Communities Built Around New Factories
q: William Lever's model village for his soap factory employees on the Mersey (1888), featuring cottages with small back gardens, was called:
n: William Lever relocated his chemical/soap factory to Port Sunlight, more of a village for his employees with cottages and small back gardens. (Source: New Communities, p.90)

q: The Spanish colonial "Plaza Complex" planning model used in the Philippines was based on the Spanish royal decree known as the:
n: The Plaza Complex was based on the "Laws of the Indies," a royal decree prescribing how colonial towns should be planned. (Source: Spanish Period, p.102)

q: The Municipal Hall (Casa Real/Ayuntamiento) in a Spanish-era plaza complex was the seat of local colonial government, representing:
n: The Municipal Hall was the seat of local colonial government, representing civil authority. (Source: Spanish Period — Key Elements, p.102)

s: New Communities Built Around New Factories
q: Titus Salt built a wooden mill town near Bradford, England (1853–1863), known as:
n: Titus Salt built Saltaire, a model industrial community with a monotonous but easily accessible layout near open country. (Source: New Communities, p.90)

q: Louis Kahn's important designs for Central Philadelphia organized circulation — main arterial stop-and-go streets and parking towers — into what he called a:
n: Kahn organized urban form into a "symphony of circulation." (Source: Louis Kahn, p.99)

q: Baron Georges-Eugène Haussmann was tasked by Napoleon III in 1853 to rebuild Paris, a project regarded as:
o: History's largest public works project at the time
n: The rebuilding of Paris entailed tearing down many houses and was history's largest public works project. (Source: Paris 1800s, p.86)

q: HSRC was renamed HLURB (Housing and Land Use Regulatory Board) in 1986, following which event?
n: HSRC was renamed HLURB in 1986 after the EDSA Revolution. (Source: Aquino Regime, p.104)

q: Biaggio Rosetti, regarded as one of the western world's earliest modern urban designers, repaired and planned the expansion of which city, considered the first modern city in Europe by 1860?
n: Rosetti repaired an existing city and planned its future expansion — Ferrara — considered the first modern city in Europe in 1860. (Source: Renaissance era entries, p.85)

q: Don Arturo Soria y Mata's 1844 proposal for a "Linear City" suggested houses and buildings be set alongside:
o: Linear utility systems supplying water, communications, and electricity
n: Soria y Mata proposed that the logic of linear utility lines should be the basis of all city layout, with houses set alongside them. (Source: 1844, p.87)

q: During the Pre-Spanish Period, Philippine settlement planning was informal and community-based, largely influenced by which two groups of settlers?
n: Planning during this time was informal and community-based, largely influenced by Chinese and Malay settlers. (Source: Pre-Spanish Period, p.102)

q: French social reformer Francois Fourier's 1829 publication, "The New World of Industry and Society," envisioned putting 400 families into a palace-like building called:
n: Fourier envisioned putting 400 families into a palace-like building he called the "Phalanstery." (Source: 1829, p.86)

q: The National Economic Council (NEC), which handled economic policy and national investment programs, was eventually merged into:
n: NEC was merged into NEDA, playing a crucial role in infrastructure and regional development planning before that. (Source: Philippine Republic, p.104)

q: Sir Christopher Wren prepared a plan for London proposing a network of avenues connecting the main features of London, including:
o: St. Peter's and St. Paul Cathedral
The Tower of London and London Bridge
n: Wren prepared a plan for London including St. Peter's and St. Paul Cathedral, proposing a network of avenues connecting London's main features. (Source: London 1600s, p.86)

s: Town & Country Planning Act of 1947 in Britain
q: A radical change in new-town concept introduced in the 1950s plan for "Hook" involved houses grouped very closely along a:
n: In the Hook plan, houses were closely grouped along a multi-level linear spine, decreasing distances to communal facilities. (Source: Town & Country Planning Act, p.95)

q: Jane Jacobs' (1962) book, one of the most influential in the history of city planning, is titled:
o: "The Death and Life of Great American Cities"
n: Jane Jacobs wrote "The Death and Life of Great American Cities." (Source: Jane Jacobs, p.100)

q: Norbert Wiener, who wrote "The Human Use of Human Beings" (1950), proposed a study of automatic control systems known as:
n: Wiener proposed cybernetics — the science of controls and communication in the animal and the machine. (Source: Norbert Wiener, p.95–96)
